City policy concerning relocation of persons displaced as a result of local land acquisition is modeled after the "Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Act of 1970", and schedules for payment to displaced persons or businesses are those outlined by the Federal Department of Housing and Urban Development. (See Apendix E) for the City of San Jose Relocation Policy.)
Since July 1, 1972, amendments to the California Government Code require that extensive relocation assistance be provided by any governmental agency acquiring property for public purposes. Consequently, the City of San Jose, in executing the Community Development Block Grant Plan, has a legal obligation to relocate each displaced household in housing complying with building and occupancy standards and having cost or rental levels that each relocated family or individual can afford.
A household qualifies for relocation assistance when it has satisfied the following conditions:
1) It occupied the property when the City made its first personal contact with the owner of the property at which time price was discussed or a written Offer To Purchase was made.
2) It vacates or moves from the property and/or removes personal property from the property as a result of project implementation.
3) The real property is purchased by the City as a part of project implementation.
The relocation plan developed by the City of San Jose contains two forms of aid to owners and tenants who must relocate. These are: (1) relocation advisory assistance in the form of counseling and aid in locating suitable replacement properties; and (2) relocation-assistance payments to help pay for the costs of relocating.
Relocating advisory assistance, to be provided by a relocation specialist, would help households to find new living accommodations by informing them about available public housing and FHA-repossessed houses, for which relocatees are given priority, and by providing current listings on properties for sale and for rent. Eligible relocatees will be given priority consideration forany housing subsidy programs that may be available.
A more substantial aid to displacees consists of the relocation assistance payments which are available. These payments are of three types.
